content.value_statement: Embedding projects often fail because model, chunking, and evaluation choices are unclear. This skill gives structured guidance for semantic search and RAG design.
actual_capabilities: Compares embedding model options by dimensions, token limits, and common use cases.
Provides OpenAI and local Sentence Transformers embedding examples.
Defines token, sentence, semantic section, and recursive chunking patterns.
Outlines domain-specific preprocessing and metadata handling for vector records.
Shows retrieval quality metrics such as precision, recall, MRR, and NDCG.
limitations: It is guidance and example code, not a complete production library.
Some examples require third-party packages, model access, or API credentials.
Model tables may need updates as embedding providers release new models.
It does not include storage integration for a specific vector database.

use_cases.title: Design a RAG ingestion pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan model selection, chunking, preprocessing, metadata, and batching for documents entering a vector index.

use_cases.title: Evaluate retrieval quality
use_cases.description: Use precision, recall, MRR, and NDCG to compare embedding and chunking choices against labeled queries.

use_cases.title: Choose embeddings for a product
use_cases.description: Compare cloud and local model options for cost, latency, multilingual support, and domain fit.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starter model
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building semantic search for [content type]. Compare embedding model options and recommend a starting model with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan chunking rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Given [document structure] and [retrieval goal], propose chunk sizes, overlap, preprocessing, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a domain pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an embedding pipeline for [domain]. Include preprocessing, metadata fields, batching, caching, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit retrieval performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my retrieval evaluation results: [metrics and examples]. Diagnose failure modes and propose model, chunking, or ranking changes.

output_examples.input: Compare embedding models for an English help center with 10,000 articles.
output: Start with a cost-effective general embedding model.
Use 512 to 800 token chunks with moderate overlap.
Evaluate recall at 10 and MRR before upgrading.

output_examples.input: Improve chunking for API docs with headings and code snippets.
output: Keep headings with their following content.
Avoid splitting code blocks across chunks.
Store section path and language as metadata.

output_examples.input: Assess retrieval results where recall is high but answers are weak.
output_examples.output: The likely issue is context quality, not only retrieval count. Review chunk boundaries, metadata filters, reranking, and answer grounding.

best_practices: Choose models based on content type, language needs, latency, and cost.
Keep chunking aligned with semantic boundaries and retrieval questions.
Measure retrieval quality with labeled queries before changing architecture.
anti_patterns: Do not mix embeddings from different models in one vector space.
Do not ignore token limits or silently truncate important context.
Do not optimize chunk size without measuring retrieval outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill generate embeddings directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example patterns that can be used with embedding libraries and APIs.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenAI and local models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for OpenAI embeddings and Sentence Transformers style local models.

faq.question: Is it only for RAG?
faq.answer: No. It also applies to semantic search, clustering, similarity scoring, and retrieval evaluation.

faq.question: Does it choose a vector database?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on embeddings, chunking, preprocessing, and evaluation before storage selection.

faq.question: How should I evaluate improvements?
faq.answer: Use labeled queries and track recall, precision, MRR, and NDCG at the target retrieval depth.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
